name: United Kingdom
summary: London is one of the world's oldest and most international markets: its history goes back to price lists at a coffee house in 1698. The FTSE 100 tracks the largest UK-listed companies. Shares trade in pounds, and buying UK shares usually costs 0.5% stamp duty.

currency.name: Pound sterling
currency.note: Many UK share prices are quoted in pence (GBX), where 100 pence make one pound. For a euro investor, moves in the pound against the euro change the value of UK shares (Category L).

source.title: FTSE Equity Country Classification Process, v3.5, October 2026, Appendix 3 (FTSE Russell, PDF)

exchanges.name: London Stock Exchange (LSE)
exchanges.hours: For SETS, the order book of the most liquid shares: opening auction 07:50–08:00, continuous trading 08:00–16:30, closing auction 16:30–16:35. On half days, continuous trading ends at 12:30.
exchanges.note: The exchange also runs AIM, a market for smaller and growing companies, founded in 1995.

indexes.name: FTSE 100
indexes.description: The largest 100 UK companies by full market capitalisation, reviewed quarterly. Launched on 3 January 1984 at 1,000 points. Calculated by FTSE Russell (LSEG).

source.title: The FTSE 100 Index: the UK's best-known equity index turns forty (FTSE Russell, PDF)

indexes.name: FTSE 250
indexes.description: The next 250 companies after the FTSE 100: the UK's mid caps. Together, the two form the FTSE 350.

source.title: The FTSE 100 Index: the UK's best-known equity index turns forty (FTSE Russell, PDF)

regulators.name: Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)
regulators.role: Regulates the conduct of around 35,500 businesses so that financial markets work well, including listing rules and market abuse.

investorProtection.name: Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS): deposits
investorProtection.text: Since 1 December 2025, deposits are protected up to £120,000 per eligible person and bank.

investorProtection.name: FSCS: investments
investorProtection.text: If an investment firm fails, eligible claims are covered up to £85,000 per person and firm (for failures after 1 April 2019). Market losses are not covered.

settlement.note: The UK moves to T+1 on the same date as the EU and Switzerland.

source.title: T+1 Settlement: SIX and the transition to T+1 (SIX)

rules.title: Stamp duty on purchases
rules.text: Buying UK shares usually costs 0.5%: Stamp Duty Reserve Tax for electronic purchases, or Stamp Duty for paper transfers over £1,000. A 1.5% rate applies to transfers into some depositary receipt schemes or clearance services.

rules.title: Prices in pence
rules.text: The London Stock Exchange quotes many shares in GBX, which means pence: a price of 2,450 GBX is £24.50. Trade values are shown in pounds.

source.title: BP plc share page, price shown in GBX (London Stock Exchange)

taxes.glance: Residents (2026–27): capital gains tax 18% or 24% above a £3,000 allowance; dividends 10.75%/35.75%/39.35% above a £500 allowance; £20,000 ISA allowance. No UK tax deducted from ordinary dividends paid to most non-residents. 0.5% stamp duty on share purchases.

items.title: Capital gains (residents)
items.text: From 6 April 2026, gains on shares are taxed at 18% within the basic-rate band and 24% above it, after a £3,000 annual tax-free allowance.

items.title: Dividends (residents)
items.text: A £500 dividend allowance; above that, 10.75% (basic rate), 35.75% (higher rate) or 39.35% (additional rate) in the 2026–27 tax year.

items.title: ISAs
items.text: UK residents can save up to £20,000 a year in ISAs, including stocks and shares ISAs, where gains and income are tax-free.

items.title: Dividends for non-residents
items.text: HMRC says UK dividend income remains non-taxable for most non-UK residents, and no UK tax is deducted from ordinary dividends. An Austrian investor pays Austrian tax on them (Category Q).

items.title: Stamp duty
items.text: Usually 0.5% when buying shares (see market rules above).

sources.title: SAIM5120: dividends received by non-UK resident persons (HMRC manual, GOV.UK)

access: Many Austrian banks and brokers offer trading on the London Stock Exchange; check costs for pound conversion and stamp duty.
Some UK-listed companies also have shares or depositary receipts traded elsewhere (Category C).
Indirectly, through funds or ETFs on the FTSE 100 or broader UK indexes (Category H).

history.text: At Jonathan's Coffee House, John Castaing begins publishing a list of stock and commodity prices.
The first regulated exchange comes into existence in London: the modern Stock Exchange is born.
The FTSE 100 is launched on 3 January at 1,000 points.
The 'Big Bang' deregulates the UK market.
On 20 October, the FTSE 100 falls 12.22%, its worst day from 1984 to 2023 (Category K).
AIM, the market for smaller growing companies, is founded.

funFacts: Of the 100 original FTSE 100 members in 1984, 26 were still in the index at the end of 2023, 12 of them under new names.
£100 invested in Reed International (now Relx) at the FTSE 100's launch would have grown to £35,393 by the end of 2023, with dividends reinvested, according to FTSE Russell.
